acl.description: List of {@link AclEntry} entries governing who can read/update/remove Objs.

parent.description: The parent reference. Overridden to be required

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

name.description: A user-defined name for a chapter in an {@link ExMachinaStory}

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

description.description: A user-defined description for a chapter in an {@link ExMachinaStory}

lastUpdated.description: When the user last modified the chapterElement by creating/editing a {@link ExMachinaStoryChapterElement}

chapterElements.description:
All elements of a chapter (named "Story Topic" in the UI) for the story. An element could be a visualization or
potentially something else in the future.

chapterElementIds.description:
An ordered array of chapter element ids in the chapter. By including this as a separate array (as opposed to using
{@link chapterElements} directly with a field to mark the sort order), we don't need to maintain and persist an
`order` field on each chapter element, which could get messy if a user frequently reorders elements because we'd
need to batch update the `order` for several elements at a time.

previewImage.description: The preview image for the chapter, which is represented by the first chapter element's preview image.

isOwned.description: If the current user owns the associated {@link ExMachinaStory}, the chapter is owned as well

title:
An {@link ExMachinaStory} is made up of {@link ExMachinaStoryChapter}s, which are called "Story Topics" in the
Ex Machina Stories UI. A story chapter can be repositioned within a story and a chapter can have multiple
{@link ExMachinaStoryChapterElement}s, which can also be repositioned within the chapter.
name: ExMachinaStoryChapter
